\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آمد} (āmad)}{آمد (āmad)}]{\ur{آمد} (āmad) — an arrival}

\label{lesson:UR-C390-amad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a yawn, then the Urdu for to doze.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آمد}}
\textbf{\ur{آمد}} — \emph{āmad} — \textquotedblleft{}an arrival\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{گاڑی} \ur{کی} \ur{آمد} \ur{شام} \ur{کو} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gāṛī kī āmad shām ko hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The train gets in this evening.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{آمد}} (\emph{āmad}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{āmad}, \textquotedblleft{}a coming\textquotedblright{}, from the verb for \textquotedblleft{}to come\textquotedblright{}; station boards list arrivals under it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmad}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gāṛī kī āmad shām ko hai.} — The train gets in this evening.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a yawn, then the Urdu for to doze, then say \emph{āmad} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{روانہ} (ravānā)}{روانہ (ravānā)}]{\ur{روانہ} (ravānā) — setting off; on its way}

\label{lesson:UR-C390-ravana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to doze, then the Urdu for an arrival.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{روانہ}}
\textbf{\ur{روانہ}} — \emph{ravānā} — \textquotedblleft{}setting off; on its way\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{گاڑی} \ur{صبح} \ur{سات} \ur{بجے} \ur{روانہ} \ur{ہوئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gāṛī subah sāt baje ravānā huī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The train set off at seven in the morning.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{روانہ}} (\emph{ravānā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{ravāna}, \textquotedblleft{}going, setting out\textquotedblright{}; with \textbf{\ur{ہونا}} it means to set off.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تاخیر} (tākhīr)}{تاخیر (tākhīr)}]{\ur{تاخیر} (tākhīr) — lateness; a delay (formal)}

\label{lesson:UR-C390-takhir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an arrival, then the Urdu for setting off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تاخیر}}
\textbf{\ur{تاخیر}} — \emph{tākhīr} — \textquotedblleft{}lateness; a delay (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بارش} \ur{کی} \ur{وجہ} \ur{سے} \ur{گاڑی} \ur{کی} \ur{آمد} \ur{میں} \ur{تاخیر} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bārish kī vajah se gāṛī kī āmad meṅ tākhīr hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The train is arriving late because of the rain.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تاخیر}} (\emph{tākhīr}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{taʾkhīr}, \textquotedblleft{}a putting off\textquotedblright{}; station announcements use it for a late train, where everyday talk says \textbf{\ur{دیر}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tākhīr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bārish kī vajah se gāṛī kī āmad meṅ tākhīr hai.} — The train is arriving late because of the rain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an arrival, then the Urdu for setting off, then say \emph{tākhīr} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{منسوخ} (mansūkh)}{منسوخ (mansūkh)}]{\ur{منسوخ} (mansūkh) — cancelled}

\label{lesson:UR-C390-mansukh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for setting off, then the Urdu for lateness.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{منسوخ}}
\textbf{\ur{منسوخ}} — \emph{mansūkh} — \textquotedblleft{}cancelled\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āj rāt kī gāṛī mansūkh ho gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{منسوخ}} (\emph{mansūkh}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{mansūkh}, \textquotedblleft{}annulled, done away with\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اتارنا} (utārnā)}{اتارنا (utārnā)}]{\ur{اتارنا} (utārnā) — to take down; to drop off}

\label{lesson:UR-C390-utaarna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for lateness, then the Urdu for cancelled.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اتارنا}}
\textbf{\ur{اتارنا}} — \emph{utārnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to take down; to drop off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{قلی} \ur{نے} \ur{ڈبے} \ur{سے} \ur{ہمارا} \ur{سامان} \ur{اتارا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qulī ne ḍabbe se hamārā sāmān utārā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The porter took our luggage down from the carriage.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{صندوق} \ur{اتارا}, \emph{us ne sandūq utārā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اتارنا}} (\emph{utārnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Hindi \emph{utārnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to take across, to make descend\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{úttarati} and its causative \emph{uttārayati} (CDIAL 1770). It is the causing partner of \textbf{\ur{اترنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to get off\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{utārnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qulī ne ḍabbe se hamārā sāmān utārā.} — The porter took our luggage down from the carriage.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for lateness, then the Urdu for cancelled, then say \emph{utārnā} again
\end{itemize}
